title: Chapter 82: The Only Witness
html:
Fan Yu visits Haunted Houses because he enjoys the company of ghosts?That improbable answer was where Doctor Gao’s reasoning led him.

“I wouldn’t diagnose him so casually. If you have the chance, bring him to see me.” Doctor Gao had never encountered a patient like this and wanted to examine him in person. “Psychological illnesses are complicated, and their causes uncertain. It could be his home environment, personal trauma, or even heredity.”

Chen Ge did not answer. The thought that Fan Yu enjoyed the company of ghosts led him to a far more frightening possibility.

He opened his raincoat and pulled Fan Yu’s drawing from his pocket: the black house and its tiny red figures.

Before arriving at Mu Yang High School, Chen Ge had assumed the drawing depicted one of its buildings. None matched, however. If anything, the squat, dilapidated home Fan Yu shared with his aunt resembled it more closely.

If Fan Yu is really drawing about the house he’s living in and these red people…Even the hairs on Chen Ge’s arms stood on end. Fan Yu’s house is filled with ghosts?!

He thought back to his visit with Fan Yu that morning. The boy had locked himself in his bedroom, door and window shut, head bowed over his drawing, while his aunt hovered outside in obvious distress.

He always used only red and black. Every picture showed a black house and red people, yet each was slightly different. The color drained from Chen Ge’s lips as he remembered that the red figures occupied different positions in every drawing.

He had dismissed those differences as childish scribbling. Now he understood: the figures recorded unclean things moving through the house.

Fan Yu can see them?

Chen Ge drew a sharp breath as more details from Fan Yu’s visit surfaced. While Chen Ge spoke to him, the boy had repeatedly stared behind him—especially at his shadow.

Fan Yu had spoken only twice inside the Haunted House, both times to Chen Ge. He had assumed the child liked him. Now he suspected the boy had recognized a kindred spirit.

No wonder he fears sunlight and loves Haunted Houses. His perception of the world has been completely warped.Chen Ge tightened his grip on the phone. He did not know what had made Fan Yu this way, but the boy’s strange behavior and his aunt’s account pointed toward a terrifying possibility.

On a similarly rainy night several years ago, the boy had disappeared. His parents met with tragedy when they went searching for him. Killing two adults and disposing of both the bodies and the evidence in a single stormy night would have required careful planning.

But viewed another way, if someone had intended to harm Fan Yu’s parents, why would a killer capable of hiding the bodies and erasing every trace of the crime let the boy live?

When his aunt said his parents had gone to heaven, Fan Yu had stared into the well and declared heaven was inside it. He knew their bodies were there. He had seen everything—he was a witness—so the killer had no reason to spare him.

Chen Ge narrowed his eyes slightly as a chill coursed through his body. That is unless the killer knew the boy or was the boy himself!

Regardless of which one it was, either possibility made Chen Ge’s heart cold with fear.

The aunt was also a prime suspect. Her story contained too many holes. She had taken far too long in the kitchen merely to pour him water, then repeatedly urged him to drink throughout their conversation and again before he left.

At the time, Chen Ge had been too focused on his mission to be careful of her ‘kindness’, but thinking back, he suspected that something had been done to that glass of water.

If the aunt killed Fan Yu’s parents, what was her motive?She loved Fan Yu enough to spoil him. Though naturally beautiful, she made no effort with her appearance, and raising him alone had clearly taken a toll. She spared no expense taking him to doctors and had put her entire life on hold for him. Could such a devoted woman truly be the killer?

To be honest, the thin woman had left a good impression on Chen Ge; he thought she was independent and strong.

Then again, if she was not the killer, the next prime suspect was the boy himself.

Fan Yu was the crime’s only witness and survivor. Chen Ge had never suspected him because he was a child, but the secret behind his drawings revealed how badly he had underestimated the boy.

Fan Yu possessed unusual eyes and lived in the constant company of ghosts. Their presence did not frighten him; he seemed perfectly at ease. Chen Ge even wondered whether the boy could control them.

The idea would sound absurd to anyone else, but Chen Ge himself was the Specter’s Favored.

But if the boy is the killer, what was his motive?This was the question that stumped Chen Ge the most. Neither the boy nor the aunt had any actual reason to murder their close family.

What really happened on that day? Fan Yu’s parents were ultimately dropped inside Mu Yang High School’s well, but why Mu Yang High School of all places?

As Chen Ge returned the drawing to his pocket, he realized the call was still connected. “I’m sorry. I got distracted.”

“No matter. I was looking through some journals for more information. His case interests me. Could you bring him to see me when you have the opportunity?” Doctor Gao had waited patiently on the line.

“Of course, should the opportunity arise, we will definitely visit you.”

“Thank you. This is my personal number, so call before you come. One last thing.” Doctor Gao hesitated, apparently weighing his next words.

“What is it?” Chen Ge was appreciative of any advice from this kind doctor.

“A patient must be treated with patience, but severe cases can pose a genuine danger. When you’re with him, take care not to provoke him.”
